title: KEDA/HPA underprovisioning during short high-velocity Redis stream bursts — learnings and runbook
creator: Maya Lin
description: During a series of customer traffic spikes on 2026-02-28 we observed sustained request latency increases and 25–40% error rate for inference routing to the Redis-backed streaming worker pool. Root cause traced to KEDA scaler failing to produce timely scale-ups for short, high-velocity bursts, combined with HPA minReplicas and pod startup latency causing underprovisioning. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and a runbook + action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-28T09:07:00Z - First alert: request 95th latency for inference-router spiked to 1.8s (baseline 220ms).
2026-02-28T09:10:00Z - Error-rate alert: 25% 5xxs for redis-stream consumer workers; SLO breach page triggered.
2026-02-28T09:12:00Z - On-call (Arjun) confirmed spike correlated with a large burst from customer ACME during a batch job. Redis stream length peaked at 4500 pending messages.
2026-02-28T09:15:00Z - Pager duty: Eng-runbook followed; attempted scale up via keda scaler but pod creation lagged and HPA did not increase replicas quickly due to average CPU metric smoothing.
2026-02-28T09:22:00Z - Manual intervention: increased HPA target and set temporary minReplicas to 8 for the worker pool; traffic recovered by 09:28Z.
2026-02-28T10:00:00Z - Post-incident triage started; collected control-plane metrics, keda scaler logs, kube-apiserver events, and pod startup traces.
root_cause: Two interacting issues caused underprovisioning: (1) KEDA Redis stream scaler poll_interval and metric aggregation window were configured with a 30s granularity and a conservative threshold, which caused the scaler to miss short-duration high-velocity bursts. (2) HPA used CPU average over a 2-minute window and a low minReplicas (2), so even when KEDA updated the custom metric, the HPA controller's smoothing delayed scale actions and the cluster's pod cold-start time (image pull + runtime init ~45–70s) meant capacity arrived too late.
impact: Customer-facing latency and error-rate SLO breaches for multiple production customers for ~10–20 minutes. No data loss. Affected requests were rerouted or retried; revenue impact estimated as low but customer experience was degraded (support tickets opened).
mitigations: Immediate: Rolled back a recent conservative KEDA threshold change pushed 2026-02-25 and temporarily raised worker pool minReplicas to 8 for critical regions.
Short-term: Reduced KEDA poll_interval to 10s for RedisStream scaler and lowered aggregation window to 15s for burst-sensitive scaler profiles.
Short-term: Adjusted HPA behavior for critical pools to use 30s metrics window and increased stabilization window settings to avoid delayed decision conflicts with KEDA.
Medium-term: Implemented a warm-pool of pre-initialized worker pods for critical customers to avoid image-pull and runtime initialization delays.
Long-term: Plan to migrate to KEDA external scaler + push metrics to kube-metrics-adapter to reduce dependency on polling and improve fidelity for sub-1min bursts.
action_items: AP-1: Update KEDA Redis scaler profiles: add 'burst-sensitive' profile with poll_interval=10s and metric_window=15s. Owner: Arjun Patel. Due: 2026-03-10.
AP-2: Implement warm-pool feature for worker pools (design + implementation + e2e tests). Owner: Priya Rao. Estimate: 13. Due: 2026-04-09.
AP-3: Add a synthetic burst test harness that generates 30–90s Redis stream storms to CI and load testing. Owner: SRE team (Ben Carter). Due: 2026-03-24.

AP-4: Create cross-check alerts: (a) KEDA metric discrepancy alert when keda_metrics != kube_metrics for same pool for >20s; (b) pod-startup-latency SLO alert. Owner: Observability (Lina Torres). Due: 2026-03-15.
AP-5: Harden HPA config for critical worker pools: set minReplicas=4 by default and reduce HPA averaging window where safe. Owner: Platform (Jared Nguyen). Due: 2026-03-18.
AP-6: Postmortem doc + customer comms draft for impacted customers with root cause and remediation steps. Owner: Maya Lin. Due: 2026-03-05.
monitoring_changes: Added Grafana dashboard panel showing KEDA scaler decisions vs Redis stream length in a single chart.
Added Prometheus alert 'KEDA_discrepancy_high' for >20s divergence between KEDA calculated metric and kube-metrics-adapter ingestion.
Added alert for pod start latency >60s for worker pools with tagging by customer tier.
Added a synthetic job in Loki that verifies KEDA logs contain scale decision entries within 15s of stream peak.
postmortem_summary: This incident highlighted fragility in our current KEDA+HPA composition for short-duration, high-velocity Redis stream workloads. KEDA's polling/aggregation parameters combined with HPA smoothing and pod cold-start time produced a gap where demand temporarily outstripped provisioned capacity. The team's immediate mitigations reduced recurrence risk; actionable work (warm-pool, improved scaler profile, synthetic tests, and monitoring) is in progress. We estimate residual risk will be low once action items are complete.
